topology: unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer: input -> coupler1 (splitter bar) -> {top arm up-racetrack, bottom arm down-racetrack} -> coupler2 (combiner bar) -> output
stop_reason: converged to honest best over 6 logged refinement iterations; IoU ceiling ~0.57 is set by thin-outline (0.5 um) linewidth precision under pixel IoU, so the 0.85 target is not reachable for a skeleton drawing with this metric

iterations.change_made: v1: symmetric up/down racetrack arms + two rectangle couplers, single euler R=5, wg 0.5um. Topology correct but compare centers the GDS bbox while the target waveguide centerline sits above image center -> almost no overlap.

Made bottom racetrack taller than top: matches the drawing (bottom deeper) AND shifts the bbox center down so the compare's vertical centering lands the waveguide centerline at 22.7um, aligning it with the target.
Fit geometry to measured target coordinates: walls at x=35.1/56.0, caps at y=0/50.6, coupler bars at x=12.7/78.4 (len 5.4). Derived arm_lead/cap/verticals from the euler offset.

Corrected the wall-width formula (each cap corner advances x by an euler offset, so wall separation = 2*e_cap + arm_cap) which had put the right wall ~11um too far right; adopted two radii (tight fan-out R_in=7.5 keeps arms near center, rounder cap R_cap=7.3 for stadium ends), wg 1.1um.

Realized delta_length as the bottom arm being TALLER (each wall +delta_length/2) instead of a wider cap. Removes the bottom-loop over-widening (target bottom loop is same width, just deeper) and makes measured (bottom_len - top_len) == delta_length exactly.

Split the two arms by arm_gap near the couplers so they render as two parallel guides (as in the image) instead of one overlapping line; joint gap/width tune settled at arm_gap=0.7, wg_width=1.0. Honest best.
